sections.h2: How fast can a Port Chester house change hands?
sections.html:
Line up the village paperwork first, then choose a buyer who can close on cash. Cash purchases drop the appraisal and loan commitment that often slow a closing, yet the deed, the state tax return and the village records still have to be finished.

Port Chester is a village within the Town of Rye in Westchester County, pressed against the Connecticut line. One sale touches the village hall, the town, the county clerk and a state tax form. The sections below take them in the order a seller meets them.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about the village itself?
sections.html:
The village's own rental registry law calls it the second most densely populated place in Westchester County after Mount Vernon. The Census Bureau counted 31,693 people in 2020 and puts the mid-2025 estimate at 32,303, within a land area of 2.33 square miles. Housing runs from one and two family houses to apartment buildings, including the former Life Savers factory, now apartments.

The village grew around the Byram River harbor and the railroad, which arrived in 1849. Steamships ran from Port Chester to New York City from 1870 until the First World War, and the Boston Post Road was one of the early routes through the settlement. Trains from the village station reach Grand Central, Stamford and New Haven, and Bee-Line routes 13 and 61 run local buses, which gives commuters a clear reason to look here.

  • Named neighborhoods include Edgewood, Traphagen and Willett Estates.
  • Every address belongs to the Port Chester-Rye Union Free School District, and the Port Chester-Rye Brook Public Library is on Haseco and Westchester Avenues.
  • The Capitol Theatre and the waterfront redevelopment anchor the downtown that buyers see first.

Winters stay moderate because the Sound takes the edge off. Wikipedia lists average annual snowfall near 30 inches, with nor'easters bringing the heavy storms, so roof, gutter and basement condition draw attention during inspections.

sections.html:
Renters slightly outnumber owners here, and the median owned home is valued at $582,600. The table uses Census Bureau QuickFacts, with five-year survey estimates ending in 2024 except where a row shows a different date.

With rent at $2,028 and an ownership rate under half, many buyers here are landlords or owner-occupants of two-family houses who plan to rent one floor. That brings in the village rental registry described next.

sections.h2: Does Port Chester have a rental registry that affects a sale?
sections.html:
Yes. Local Law I-5 of 2023 created Chapter 248, a registry for two-family dwellings that are rented and not owner-occupied. If one unit is owner-occupied or the house is vacant, no certificate is required.

  • A rental registry certificate lasts two years, and renewal papers are due 45 days ahead of the expiration date.
  • The certificate cannot be transferred. Anyone buying a rented two-family and keeping the tenants needs a new certificate when title closes.
  • The owner must tell the Department of Code Enforcement right away about a change in status, and the law names an impending sale as one example.
  • The application costs $75, which covers the village inspection. Each re-inspection costs $150.
  • To register, the property needs no open code cases, no pending village enforcement proceedings, and current village taxes and special assessments.

Violations draw a fine of $500 to $5,000, up to 15 days in jail, or both penalties. If you own a tenant-occupied two-family house, ask the village whether your certificate is current before a buyer's attorney asks for it.

sections.h2: What does the Port Chester Building Department handle before closing?
sections.html:
The Building Department issues permits, schedules inspections, resolves notices of violation and handles the Municipal Search Report. The search request form is submitted with a check made out to the Village of Port Chester.

The permit counter takes walk-ins on weekdays from 9 am to 1 pm, and phone messages are checked from 9 am to 4 pm. Permit records since February 2021 are digital in the village's Accela portal, while older files require a Freedom of Information request to the village clerk. One question on New York's disclosure form asks whether certificates of occupancy exist for the property, so an owner with an unpermitted porch, finished basement or extra kitchen should learn now what the file shows.

New York revised its statewide building and energy codes, and the new edition took effect December 31, 2025. Work permitted years ago was inspected under older rules, and the department can explain what that means for a permit still open.

sections.h2: What village bills come up when a Port Chester house is sold?
sections.html:
Sewer rent is the one many owners overlook. The village bills it apart from property tax, based on metered water use, with invoices mailed about every three months. A bill must be paid inside 25 days, a 1% penalty follows, and unpaid sewer rent attaches to the parcel as a lien under General Municipal Law section 452.

According to the village FAQ, when a property changes ownership the village and the water billing authority must be notified before the title closing, so a final reading can be taken and the new owner recorded. Do this early, since a missing final reading can hold up the payoff figure.

Your annual tax bill also carries a Port Chester Sewer Tax collected for Westchester County's treatment plant, a different charge from the village sewer rent. Get a written payoff from the village or your attorney so each charge shows up in the closing adjustments.

sections.h2: How is a Port Chester deed recorded and what tax is due?
sections.html:
Port Chester deeds are recorded by the Westchester County Clerk. The clerk takes a deed only with a PREP-generated cover page, Form TP-584, Form RP-5217 and a payment cover page showing fees and taxes.

  • Recording: $45 for the deed, $5 per page, and $5 to file the TP-584.
  • RP-5217 filing: $125 for residential property. The clerk's own illustration prices a three-page residential deed covering one municipality at $190.
  • State transfer tax: two dollars per $500 of price, with the price rounded up. A $404,501 sale is treated as $405,000 and owes $1,620.
  • Mansion tax: an extra 1% on a home that sells for a million dollars or more, owed by the buyer.

Under the Tax Department's rules the seller carries the base tax by default, and the return and payment are due within 15 days of the deed's delivery. A seller living outside New York must also deal with estimated income tax on the gain at filing.

sections.h2: What does New York require a Port Chester seller to disclose?
sections.html:
Section 462 of the Real Property Law makes the seller of a house with up to four dwelling units sign a condition disclosure form and put it in the buyer's hands ahead of a binding contract. The same statute permits an "as is" sale, so the form and a discounted price can sit side by side.

For a house close to the water, read the flood questions with care. They ask about FEMA floodplain mapping, any flood insurance policy, and water that reached the basement from heavy rain or tidal flooding. A knowingly false or incomplete answer can expose the seller to claims before or after title passes.

faqs.q: Must a landlord register a two-family before selling it?
faqs.a: Only if it is rented and non-owner-occupied. The certificate cannot be transferred, so the buyer applies for a new one at closing, and code enforcement should hear about the pending sale.

faqs.q: Who bears the state transfer tax here?
faqs.a: The seller owes the base tax by default, and a contract can shift it. The buyer owes the 1% mansion tax at $1 million or more.

faqs.q: Which office records a Port Chester deed?
faqs.a: The Westchester County Clerk, through its PREP system. You need the deed, a TP-584, an RP-5217 and payment of the recording fee and taxes.

faqs.q: Will unpaid sewer rent follow the house to the buyer?
faqs.a: It can, because the unpaid amount attaches to the parcel. Ask the village for a final reading and a payoff figure ahead of closing so the adjustments cover it.

faqs.q: Can a house with open repairs still be sold in Port Chester?
faqs.a: Yes. New York allows as-is sales, but you still must hand over the signed disclosure statement before the buyer signs, and any open permits or violations are best sorted with the Building Department.
